title: Infrastructure as code (Terraform/OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Pulumi)
appliesWhen: Cloud or platform infrastructure is defined in code in this repository (Terraform or OpenTofu, AWS CloudFormation/SAM/CDK, Pulumi) and applied to real environments.
ask: Will infrastructure be defined in code here? Which tool (Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation/CDK, Pulumi), where is state kept, and who or what applies changes?

sources.title: Terraform: manage sensitive data (ephemeral values, write-only arguments)

guidance: tfsec is no longer the recommended scanner: Aqua folded it into Trivy, whose `trivy config` scans Terraform, CloudFormation, Azure ARM, Helm, Kubernetes and Dockerfiles. Checkov (`checkov -d .`) is an alternative; either is fine, pick one and keep it.

Trivy's release pipeline was compromised in March 2026 (GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23, CVE-2026-33634): binary v0.69.4 and aquasecurity/trivy-action before 0.35.0 and setup-trivy before 0.2.6 were affected. Pin Trivy and its actions to a current release by version and checksum or commit SHA, never a floating tag.

terraform validate needs an initialised directory; `terraform init -backend=false` initialises without touching the remote backend, so it is safe in CI. Run fmt and validate in every root module; with several root modules, loop over them in the gate command.

For OpenTofu, use `tofu fmt -check -recursive` and `tofu validate`; OpenTofu can also encrypt state client-side. For CloudFormation use cfn-lint and change sets; for Pulumi use the language's type check and `pulumi preview`. Replace the Terraform commands with profile gate … --command.

Values marked sensitive are still written to state and plan files. Keep secrets out of state with ephemeral values (Terraform 1.10+) and write-only arguments (1.11+) where the provider supports them, or let the cloud generate and hold the secret (managed passwords in a secrets manager).
S3 backend: set use_lockfile = true for native locking (DynamoDB locking is deprecated), encrypt = true (and kms_key_id for a customer key), and enable bucket versioning and restricted access.
Commit .terraform.lock.hcl and pin required_version and provider versions so plans are reproducible.
Pitfall: applying from a laptop. Apply from CI using the reviewed saved plan, with an identity that only the pipeline can assume.

gates.title: Infrastructure code is formatted
gates.architecture: Record the IaC tool and version (Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, Pulumi), the repository layout of root modules and reusable modules, and the formatting check used.
acceptance: terraform fmt -check -recursive (or the tool's equivalent) exits 0

gates.title: Infrastructure code validates
gates.setup: Run from the root module directory; with several root modules or a subfolder (for example infra/), change the command with profile gate G-IAC-VALIDATE --command "…".
gates.architecture: Record the pinned tool and provider versions (required_version, required_providers, committed .terraform.lock.hcl) and which root modules are validated.
acceptance: terraform validate (or the tool's equivalent) succeeds for every root module
Tool and provider versions are pinned and the dependency lock file is committed

gates.title: No high or critical misconfigurations in infrastructure code
gates.setup: Install a pinned, current Trivy release (not v0.69.4). To use Checkov instead, set profile gate G-IAC-SCAN --command "checkov -d . --quiet". Accept a finding only with an inline ignore that states the reason.
gates.architecture: Record the misconfiguration scanner and its version, the severity threshold, and how accepted findings are documented (inline ignore with reason and owner).
acceptance: The scanner reports no high or critical findings, or each remaining one has a documented ignore with a reason
The scan runs in CI on every change to infrastructure code

gates.title: State stored remotely with locking, encryption and restricted access
gates.architecture: Record the state backend, locking mechanism, encryption at rest (and key), versioning or backups of state, one state per environment, and who and which pipelines can read or write state.
acceptance: No state files are committed to the repository (*.tfstate and .terraform/ are ignored)
Remote state has locking enabled, is encrypted at rest and versioned, and only the deploy pipeline and named operators can access it
Each environment has its own state

gates.title: Least-privilege IAM defined in code
gates.architecture: Record the roles and policies the code creates, the identity that runs plan and apply (separate read-only plan role if possible, OIDC federation from CI rather than stored keys), and the rule against wildcard actions and resources.
acceptance: Policies created by the code grant specific actions on specific resources; any wildcard is documented with a reason
CI authenticates to the cloud with short-lived federated credentials, not stored access keys

gates.title: No secrets in infrastructure code or state
gates.architecture: Record how secrets used by infrastructure are created and passed (secrets manager references, cloud-managed passwords, ephemeral values or write-only arguments) so they do not appear in code, variables files, plans or state.
acceptance: No secret values appear in .tf/.tfvars or template files, plan output or state
Variables and outputs that carry sensitive values are marked sensitive or ephemeral

gates.title: Resources are tagged consistently
gates.architecture: Record the required tags or labels (for example owner, environment, application, cost centre, data classification) and how they are applied by default (provider default_tags or a shared module).
acceptance: Every taggable resource carries the required tags, applied by default in code

gates.title: Plans reviewed before apply
gates.architecture: Record the change workflow: plan in CI on every pull request, plan output attached to the review, apply only from CI with the reviewed saved plan, approval required for production, and drift detection.
acceptance: Every infrastructure change has a plan reviewed by someone other than the author before apply
Production applies run from CI using the reviewed plan, not from personal machines
Drift between code and real infrastructure is detected on a schedule
